answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable token as a bond before bidding, and slash that bond when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud. Sybil accounts are still possible, but an attacker must buy and immobilize a separate token for every persona, then risks losing them all; creating names is cheap, multiplying influence is not. Even at a summit, a sable-branded agent cannot forge its way around the same collateral rule.
